evidence: src/users/infrastructure/persistence/user.repository.ts declares only `export abstract class UserRepository`. Its methods are create, findManyWithPagination, findById, findByIds, findByEmail, findBySocialIdAndProvider, update and remove, and all of them operate on User.
Every method signature is typed against the User domain model (e.g. `findById(id: User['id']): Promise<NullableType<User>>`), so one abstraction is used throughout.

The graph shows UsersDocumentRepository and UsersRelationalRepository with IMPLEMENTS edges to UserRepository, and UsersService with a CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS edge to it. That makes it the one shared contract, with no rules defined in more than one place.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This unit is a single file that declares one abstract class, UserRepository. The class is the persistence port for the User aggregate. All of its members deal with one concern: storing and fetching User entities. It uses the domain abstraction (User, User['id'] and similar) the same way throughout. It holds no implementation logic, so no rule or invariant is repeated, and it does not route around any of the module's own abstractions. The document and relational repositories both implement it, and UsersService injects it, so it works as the module's single contract. It does use FilterUserDto and SortUserDto from the application DTOs, but that is a layer-dependency question, which is out of scope here.
